answer.answer: Straylight is not ready for dependable owner use at 10× corpus growth. The 2026-07-26 current-status note supersedes the older green checkpoint: connection, authentication, and exact-path reads work, but production-scale retrieval can time out, transaction coupling can discard a successful lane, and normal writes copy the full membership manifest. At the owner corpus scale of about 64,000 active records and 9.6 million estimated source tokens, exact-path reads work, but broad `memory.open` and lexical retrieval are slow and can hit the 30-second database timeout. Because retrieval lanes share one transaction, a later lane failure can also cause the result from an earlier successful lane to be lost.

Normal writes copy a full corpus membership manifest, creating write amplification tied to the entire corpus rather than only the changed material. This production-sized full-manifest-copy finding is part of why the current architecture is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth.

Connection, authentication, and exact-path reads work, but these broad-retrieval mechanisms prevent dependable owner readiness at 10x corpus growth.

Normal writes copy a full corpus membership manifest. This makes each ordinary write amplify with corpus-wide membership state rather than only the changed files, contributing to the conclusion that the current architecture is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth.

The approved direction is to make current Markdown files the workspace truth; version only changed files; make indexes and derived views rebuildable; checkpoint with exact path, version, and hash references plus changes since a workspace generation; and retain coherent source hydration and compact retrieval packets. This is the approved proposal, not evidence that it has already been implemented or production-verified.
